original_question: Let F be a foliation of degree d ≥ 2 with non-hyperbolic singularities. Describe the directed positive ddc-closed currents of F, and determine when F can admit diffuse positive closed currents directed by the foliation.
target_in_paper: Problem 3.2 in Section 3 (Unique ergodicity for foliations), read together with the Section 1 definitions of degree and directed dd^c-closed currents, and with Theorem 3.1 as the solved hyperbolic comparison case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target: it correctly focuses on a degree-d foliation with non-hyperbolic singularities, asks for a description of directed positive dd^c-closed currents, and separately asks when diffuse positive closed directed currents can exist. That is essentially the content of Problem 3.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: The ambient space is the complex projective plane P^2(C), not an unspecified manifold or surface; Section 3 says the paper states the result only in the P^2 case for simplicity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
F should be a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces on P^2(C). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The degree is the geometric degree defined in Section 1 via a homogeneous polynomial vector field on C^3 descending to P^2, and interpreted as the number of tangencies with a generic projective hyperplane. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
Problem 3.2 itself does not impose the extra restriction d >= 2; that lower bound is added by the draft and is not paper-faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Directed positive dd^c-closed currents are currents of bidimension (1,1) satisfying T wedge alpha = 0 for local holomorphic 1-forms alpha defining the foliation; Section 1 also recalls dd^c = (i/pi) partial bar-partial. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The problem asks for all such directed positive dd^c-closed currents, not only extremal ones and not only currents normalized to mass 1; the mass-1 normalization appears in Theorem 3.1, not in Problem 3.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Hyperbolic singularity is defined nearby as one for which the quotient of the eigenvalues of the linearized defining vector field is non-real, so non-hyperbolic must be understood relative to that definition. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
Diffuse should be made explicit: the paper says a current is diffuse if it gives no mass to analytic varieties. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The immediate local context matters for the exact scope: near hyperbolic singularities local positive closed currents are supported on separatrices, while at a non-degenerate singularity with real eigenvalue quotient the local space of directed positive closed currents is large; the unresolved issue is global existence/classification. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
refined_question: Let F be a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces of geometric degree d on the complex projective plane P^2(C), having at least one non-hyperbolic singularity, where a singularity is called hyperbolic when the quotient of the eigenvalues of the linearized defining vector field is non-real. Describe all positive dd^c-closed currents of bidimension (1,1) directed by F, in the sense that T wedge alpha = 0 for every local holomorphic 1-form alpha defining F and dd^c = (i/pi) partial bar-partial. Also determine for which such foliations there exist diffuse positive closed directed currents, where diffuse means giving no mass to analytic varieties. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 3.2 almost verbatim, rather than a neighboring statement. Theorem 3.1 gives the completed hyperbolic case in P^2 and therefore supplies the comparison that motivates Problem 3.2. Section 1 provides the hidden notation needed to make the question stand alone, namely the meaning of degree, directed current, and dd^c. The paragraphs immediately after Problem 3.2 explain why the question is specifically about non-hyperbolic singularities: the local positive closed currents are rigid in the hyperbolic case but plentiful in certain non-hyperbolic local models, while the global classification remains unclear. The paper also notes a nearby coexistence question about having both diffuse positive closed currents and diffuse non-closed dd^c-closed currents, but it does not present that as an equivalent reformulation of Problem 3.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
